sections.html: The flag cichlid, Mesonauta festivus, is a cichlid recorded from Venezuela, Peru, Brazil, Bolivia and Paraguay. It lives in well planted, slower-moving waters. Flag cichlids are found in most aquatic stores, but the fish usually sold under the name is M. insignis. It is peaceful, but becomes more aggressive when breeding.

Widespread through much of South America, it's been recorded from Peru, Brazil, Bolivia and Paraguay. It's found in numerous river drainages, including the Rio Tapajós, Rio Jamari, Rio Madre de Dios, Rio Guaporé, Rio Mamoré, Rio Paraguay and Rio Paraná.
Usually found in well planted habitats in slower moving waters.
Standard length: 100 mm SL (3.9 in). Aquarium base: 120 × 38 cm (48 × 15 in). Volume: ~137 litres (~36 US gal), for a tank of 120 × 38 × 30 cm.
Well planted tank with moderate water flow. Bogwood and branches can be used for decor. Sandy substrate is preferred. Lighting should not be too strong.

• Temperature: 24–28°C. Occurs in a wide range of temperatures in the wild; 24–28°C (76–82°F) is suggested in the aquarium.
  • pH: 6.0–8.0 will be tolerated but a pH of around 6.5 is suggested.
  • Hardness: up to 5 dGH.

It's a generalistic omnivore by nature. Wild fish feed on worms, crustaceans, plant matter (apparently including algae) and other zoobenthos. Accepts the majority of prepared foods. This should be supplemented with live foods such as bloodworm and brineshrimp and some vegetable matter.

Peaceful cichlid, although becomes more aggressive when breeding. Can be kept with other peaceful cichlids such as geophagus and apistogramma and other peaceful community species such as tetras, barbs and small catfish.
Male is larger and has extensions to the dorsal and anal fins.

Breeding takes place on a flat stone or similar area. Once the breeding area is prepared, eggs will be deposited by the female and then fertilised by the male. In excess of 200 eggs may be laid. Both fish guard the eggs and when the fry hatch two to three days later, they are transferred to a pit where the parents keep them until they become free-swimming. This is usually 3–4 days after hatching. Both fish assume parental duties but can be easily spooked, often leading to them eating the fry. It is advisable that the breeding tank be placed in a quiet location and disturbed as little as possible. Fry can be fed on newly-hatched brineshrimp and powdered fry foods until large enough to take bigger foods.

Flag Cichlids are enduringly popular in the hobby and can be found in most aquatic stores. Interestingly, this species is not the species most commonly sold as the Flag cichlid. It is usually M. insignis that makes it into dealers' tanks.
